chunks: "Dielectric loss is energy turned into heat inside the insulating material of the line. Physically the dielectric has bound charges and molecular dipoles.
When the field alternates they try to follow it, but they can't respond instantly, so the polarization lags the field by a small angle.
Because of that lag, some of the energy put into polarizing the material each cycle isn't returned; it's dissipated as heat.
Mathematically that's the imaginary part of the permittivity, and the ratio of imaginary to real parts is the loss tangent, delta .
In a transmission line it shows up as a shunt conductance, G' equals omega C' delta , so the attenuation from the dielectric is about alpha d about pi f square root of r delta over c .
